name: Ambrisentan
drug_class: Selective endothelin type A receptor antagonist
route_note: Oral tablet once daily, alone or with tadalafil
originator: Knoll (BASF Pharma, later Abbott); developed by Myogen

discovery.note: A propanoic acid ETA-selective antagonist later licensed to Myogen, which Gilead acquired in 2006. Year of first patent filing (priority October 1994, BASF, US 5,932,730).

rx_status: prescription (restricted programme for pregnancy risk in the US)
tagline: Once-daily ETA-selective endothelin antagonist for pulmonary arterial hypertension
summary: Ambrisentan is a selective endothelin type A receptor antagonist taken once daily for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Started together with tadalafil, it reduces clinical failure compared with either drug alone.
mechanism: Ambrisentan blocks the ETA receptor on pulmonary vascular smooth muscle, preventing endothelin-1-induced vasoconstriction and proliferation.
Sparing ETB receptors may preserve endothelin clearance and endothelial nitric oxide and prostacyclin release, although the clinical importance of selectivity is debated.
uses: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO group I), alone or in combination with tadalafil

history.title: Gilead acquires Myogen
history.detail: Gilead gains ambrisentan through its acquisition of Myogen.

history.title: Liver warning removed
history.detail: FDA removes the boxed warning on liver injury; embryo-fetal toxicity warning remains.

history.title: AMBITION
history.detail: Initial ambrisentan plus tadalafil is shown to reduce clinical failure; FDA approves the combination use.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic ambrisentan becomes available in the US.

safety.boxed_warning: Embryo-fetal toxicity; do not use in pregnancy; available in the US only through a restricted programme.

facts: Ambrisentan is contraindicated in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis after a trial (ARTEMIS-IPF) was stopped for harm.
It was one of Gilead's first non-antiviral products.
